issue.title: Flaky test_commit_sdd_files_waits_for_store_write_lock: 50ms thread window is too tight under CI load
issue.description:
Found by a CI-repair agent while diagnosing the pinned master failure on 222dd1e26; NOT caused by that work (tests-only change to tests/ace/tui/test_agent_metadata_search.py).

FAILURE (GitHub Actions, sase-org/sase master 22c41c0a2, run 31146528069 job 'test (3.12)' coverage leg, gw2, Python 3.12.13, 1 failed / 26,680 passed / 46 skipped in 1529.82s):

  tests/test_sdd_commit.py::test_commit_sdd_files_waits_for_store_write_lock
  E  assert True is False
  +  where True = is_alive()
  +    where is_alive = <Thread(Thread-338 (commit_in_thread), stopped 140116410144448)>.is_alive

Note the repr: by the time pytest rendered the traceback the writer thread was already 'stopped'. The thread was alive only at the instant the assertion sampled it, which is the signature of a too-tight timing window rather than a real lock-ordering defect.

MECHANISM (read from the test source in the CI log, not reproduced under load): the test sets ENV_STORE_WRITE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=1, holds store_git_write_lock(repo), starts commit_in_thread() which calls commit_sdd_files(), waits on started.wait(timeout=1), then does a bare time.sleep(0.05) before asserting the writer has not progressed. Every margin in the test is a fixed sub-second real-time sleep against a 1s lock timeout. On a contended 28-worker runner (this run took 25.5 minutes of wall clock) 50ms is not a reliable barrier, and the 1s store-lock timeout can itself expire while the main thread is descheduled, letting the writer finish early.

DISTINCT from the two flake beads already open:
- sase-ct is scoped to ACE TUI pilot/pump tests; this is a non-ACE threading test with no Textual pilot involved.
- sase-gl is the cached_baselines mtime tie-break; unrelated code and unrelated mechanism.

SCOPE: reproduce under artificial load, then replace the real-time sleeps with a deterministic barrier - have the writer signal that it has actually entered the lock wait (or poll for the lock-wait state) instead of sleeping 50ms and inferring it, and assert on observed state transitions rather than on is_alive() sampled at a fixed instant. Widening the sleep is not a fix, only a wider flake window.

No credible link to in-progress epic sase-gn/sase-gn.10 (snoozed task beads and the snooze close-path repair): that work changes bead-store close/snooze mutation semantics, while this test exercises the SDD git-commit path's wait on store_git_write_lock and fails on thread timing, not on any store error.
